messages:
maya: heads up — saw a sharp regression in eval metrics after yesterday's quantized Llama3 bring-up on main. exact-match down ~6% on our QA suite. CI eval job failing intermittently.
ci-bot: eval-ci: job 412 failed on commit 9fc7d2a (author: oliver). 12/68 evals failed. logs: https://ci.redwood.example/runs/412
raj: can you paste the failing metric lines? rough counts are fine.
maya: logs: 
```
[eval] squad_exact_match: baseline=79.4 -> current=73.5
[eval] rouge_l: baseline=44.1 -> current=39.8
```
oliver: hmm I landed a small change to runner cache eviction heuristics in that commit when fixing long-running KV cache leaks. patch: `runner.cache_ttl = 0` -> allowed immediate eviction for idle sessions. didn't expect evals to rely on persistent prefix caching.
raj: I started a quick bisect between v3.2.1 and HEAD. first bad commit points to 9fc7d2a (oliver) — matches.
ash (sre-bot): added label `release-blocker` to PR #7802 referenced by commit 9fc7d2a.
ash (ashley): if eviction caused missing prefix KV, quantized models will produce different tokenization/continuation patterns. could explain metric drift.
julien: are we sure it's not the quantization recipe change? that also rolled yesterday in the same release window.
maya: timeline: quantization PR merged at 02:14, runtime eviction change merged at 02:42, first failing CI at 03:10. looks correlated with eviction change.
raj: can we reproduce locally? trying a two-run comparison with and without cache_ttl=0 on the same quantized checkpoint.
oliver: quick diff of my change: 
```
- # previous defaults
- runner.cache_ttl = 10  # seconds
+ # aggressive eviction to reduce mem pressure
+ runner.cache_ttl = 0
```
raj: ran local evals with the quantized model. with ttl=10 -> exact_match 79.2, ttl=0 -> 73.6. reproduces.
nash (ci-bot): attaching reduced repro config: `./tools/eval_runner --suite=qa_small --model=llama3-q8 --cache-ttl=0`
ash (ashley): suggestion: revert the eviction change in runtime and do a targeted memory patch. we can't ship this with observable regressions.
julien: alternative is rollback the model quantization rollout, but that loses q8 perf improvements. which has lower risk?
maya: rolling back runtime change is smaller and quick. it was a single-line config change.
oliver: I can ship a revert PR in 10 min. also will add a safeguard test in eval CI to detect cache-dependent regressions (run small prefix-persistence test).
raj: agree on revert + test. we should also add a canary that runs quantized model evals with both aggressive and conservative ttl to catch future breakage.
nash (sre-bot): release status: hold current deploy. marking release channel and notifying PM on-call.
nash (ci-bot): opened issue #9423: "eval regression caused by runner cache_ttl=0" and linked PR #7810 as revert candidate.
ash (ashley): assign oliver to revert PR, raj to add CI test, maya to validate after revert. target: revert merged + green CI within 2h.
oliver: starting PR now. thanks for the quick triage. :thumbsup:
raj: I'll add a small unit test that runs a short seq2seq with a reused prefix and asserts identical outputs between cached and non-evicted runs. will add to eval CI gating.
maya: after revert I'll re-run full QA suite and post results here.
julien: good call on canary CI. we should also add a metric-alert rule for >3% drop in top-level suites during rollout.
maya: noted. creating alert ticket.
nash (ci-bot): CI status: revert PR #7810 created by oliver, tests running.
maya: thanks team. keeping release on hold until we confirm fixes.
raj: putting a short postmortem stub in #postmortems after we close the incident.
oliver: if anything blocks the revert ping me, I'll stay on it.
nash (sre-bot): participants notified: oncall, release-manager, product.
